description:
## Empirical signal (2026-05-04)

Surfaced during ariadne--m20 + the-stoa team install coordination. User-tier POLYBIUS proposed a coordination pattern that had workspace POLYBIUS polling u-- (user-tier beadwork) for messages — violating the asymmetric scoping that keeps each tier's working memory bounded. PRINCIPAL caught it: 'I thought it was only a downward permissions and you can write to all but the level below you can write to their level or a shared level with those below them?'

The model is correct, but the substrate's documentation (§7.1 of MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md) discusses VISIBILITY (read access) but does not explicitly state the WRITE rules. User-tier POLYBIUS got the read model right (project-tier doesn't read user-tier) but inferred the wrong write pattern (suggesting workspace POLYBIUS could write to u-- by polling it).

The implied-but-unstated write rule is:

| Seat | Reads | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| User-tier POLYBIUS | u-- + all project-tier (downward) | u-- + all project-tier (downward) |
| Project-tier (workspace, sub-project) | own project bw | own project bw |

**Cross-tier coordination always meets in the lower tier's bw.** User-tier descends to coordinate; project-tier never ascends.

## What needs to change in substrate

1. **Update MAJOR_POLYBIUS §7.1** to make the write rules explicit alongside the visibility rules. Add a table or explicit bullets covering both read and write at each tier.

2. **Add a 'cross-tier coordination pattern' subsection** explicitly stating: 'When a user-tier seat coordinates with a project-tier seat, the meeting point is the project-tier bw. User-tier writes down; project-tier never writes up.' With an example (e.g., the ariadne--m20 radio-check pattern from 2026-05-04 as anchor).

3. **Update MAJOR_PLINY** if PLINY has any bw-write conventions that need parallel clarification — quick check, may be no-op.

4. **Cross-ref from operating-disciplines.md** if appropriate (this is universal team protocol, not POLYBIUS-specific).

## Why this matters

The asymmetric scoping is what keeps each tier's working memory bounded. If project-tier seats start writing to u-- (or polling it), they accumulate cross-project context they don't need (other projects' tickets, user-tier discipline accretion, retrospectives). That defeats the bounded-context property the per-tier separation provides.

User-tier POLYBIUS captured this as a feedback memory locally (~/.claude/projects/.../memory/feedback_bw_visibility_is_downward_only.md), but feedback memories don't propagate to other POLYBIUS instances. The pattern needs to be substrate canon so every deployed POLYBIUS inherits the explicit rules.

## Sequencing

This is a documentation-only substrate update — no install.sh changes needed. After it lands at substrate, install re-runs at deployed tiers (workspace + sub-project + the-stoa) propagate the updated role file.

DAEDALUS to design the §7.1 expansion shape; ARGUS to critique whether the table or bullet form is clearer; ADA to write; VERA to verify content-preservation; CATO to review craft; ZENO to spec-check against current §7.1 text.

## Related substrate tickets (POLYBIUS-pair coordination protocol family)

- stoa--vz9 (operating disciplines, landed)
- stoa--ivc (radio-check pattern)
- stoa--ay1 (adaptive polling cadence)
- THIS TICKET (cross-tier write boundaries explicit)

POLYBIUS_the_stoa may want to bundle these into a single arc covering POLYBIUS-pair coordination protocol comprehensively, or sequence them. Worth discussing at arc-21 directive design time.

## Reference

- §7.1 of substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md (current text — visibility only)
- ariadne--m20 (2026-05-04 engagement that surfaced this)
- ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/feedback_bw_visibility_is_downward_only.md (user-tier local capture, to be promoted to substrate)
title: Make bw cross-tier write boundaries explicit in substrate (currently implicit in §7.1 visibility text)
